title: Event Canonicalizer: robust ingestion + schema hub for console usage events
creator: Anika Rao
description: Goal: replace fragmented validation logic across console backend services with a single Event Canonicalizer service and a versioned Schema Hub. The canonicalizer handles fast-path validation for high-volume usage events (UI interactions, API calls, cost telemetry) and a slow-path enrichment/repair pipeline for malformed or legacy payloads.
design_notes: We standardize on a JSON Schema + small mapping shim approach: schemas are authored in the Schema Hub (git-backed registry), each schema has semantic versioning (major.minor.patch). Incoming events are routed to either: 1) fast-path validator (strict, drop or reject bad messages for real-time metrics) or 2) slow-path normalizer (attempts field mapping, type coercion, and enrichment by calling legacy-mapping functions). For compatibility we support 'legacy-mode' mappings declared per-project. Canonicalizer is a horizontally scalable Go microservice with non-blocking validation using a compiled schema cache and a short-lived worker pool for slow-path async repairs. We will persist raw events to the raw-topic for replayability and store canonicalized payloads in the cleaned-topic for downstream consumers (analytics, billing, and cost dashboards).
acceptance_criteria: Schema Hub supports registering schemas with change log and tags
Event Canonicalizer validates 99.95% of fast-path events under 75ms median validation latency at 50k eps
Malformed events are routed to slow-path and repaired automatically for >70% of known legacy formats
All canonicalized events include metadata: schema_id, schema_version, canonicalizer_version, validation_status
End-to-end e2e test harness that replays historical 7 days of raw events and agrees with production analytics outputs within 0.5%
implementation_plan: 1) Schema Hub: git-backed registry + API + admin UI; implement authoring API and RBAC hooks (week 1)
2) Canonicalizer service: implement fast-path compiled validator + kafka consumer and producer (week 2)
3) Slow-path normalizer: implement repair worker and mapping library; integrate enrichment functions (week 3)
4) Integration: update console-ingress to forward raw events to raw-topic and add schema_id hints where available (week 3)
5) Observability: add tracing, per-schema metrics, histogram of validation latency, and dashboards (week 3)
6) Rollout: dark traffic run for 72 hours, compare analytics, then gradual 25/50/100% cutover (week 4)
rollout_plan: Start with a dark-run in us-west for 72 hours using sampling of 100% raw traffic but writing canonical events to a dark topic. Validate downstream consumers against dark-topic. If discrepancies <= 0.5% and latency/throughput targets are met, proceed with a canary for dashboard-critical schemas (billing, usage) to 25% of production traffic for 24 hours. Expand to 50% and then 100% with automated rollback if validation-error-rate exceeds 1% or canonicalization latency percentiles breach SLOs.
comments: 2026-01-14: Initial design review completed. Decision: JSON Schema for developer ergonomics, compiled cache for fast path. - Anika
2026-01-20: Prototype validator implemented (Go + ajv-like compiled library). Benchmarks: 60k eps on a n2-standard-8 equivalent instance with median validation latency 22ms. - Marco

2026-01-25: Discovered edge case: nested arrays with heterogeneous element types used by legacy billing events. Decided to add per-schema transform hooks and a 'legacy_event_v1' mapping table to avoid broad schema relaxations. - Design/Eng sync
2026-01-30: PR for Schema Hub API opened; awaiting security review for RBAC endpoints. - Priya

2026-02-02: Dark-run configured for us-west cluster; started collecting canonicalization diffs. Initial mismatch rate 1.8% primarily due to timestamp format differences; adding timestamp normalizer in slow-path. - Marco
